newsitem.title: DENMARK: Quiet Danish shares slip a little, outlook unsure.
newsitem.headline: Quiet Danish shares slip a little, outlook unsure.

text.p: Danish share prices closed marginally lower on Thursday hit by late afternoon selling out of key paper in a thin, pre-Christmas market, with dealers unsure of trends up to the weekend.

"Investors are very much on the sidelines at the moment, most of them have closed their books for this year and gone off on holiday. The KFX December future's expiry late tomorrow morning should brighten the market up," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 0.18 point lower at 130.97 in overall bourse turnover of 1.029 billion crowns.
Dealers said overnight U.S. trends and the expiry of the December future would set the course for the market on Friday.
The KFX December future fell a negligible 0.05 point to 130.65 with 711 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
SAS Denmark was the most traded paper of the day with 241,000 shares changing hands to close one crown up at 74.

Den Danske Bank finished three crowns down at 452, with rival Unidanmark unchanged at 297. Danisco rose three to 341 after its good interim result, ISS put on the same to end at 157 in the wake of the sale of its U.S. ISS Inc unit.
